claim: Stability AI confirmed hands are underrepresented in training datasets and appear smaller in source images than faces
quote: Hands also tend to be much smaller in the source images, as they are relatively rarely visible in large form.

claim: Occlusion in training data causes models to learn that thumbs are 'sometimes absent' rather than hidden, producing deformed outputs
quote: When it reproduces it, it's somewhat deformed — the rest of it is hidden under fabric or grabbing onto something.

claim: Prof. Peter Bentley (UCL) explains 2D generators have no concept of 3D hand geometry
quote: These are 2D image generators that have absolutely no concept of the three-dimensional geometry of something like a hand.

claim: LAION-5B training images lack detailed hand descriptions in captions; hands fall into the uncanny valley for human observers
quote: This image doesn't add information to describe what his normal hands look like: his hand is in a relaxed position.

claim: HandRefiner paper: hands have 16 joints and 27 degrees of freedom; 3D-to-2D projection ambiguity causes incorrect finger counts; depth-conditioned inpainting achieved 70% user preference in blind surveys
quote: A kinematic model of hand contains 16 joints and 27 degrees of freedom. Occlusions from varying viewpoints make it difficult to determine finger ordering and visibility.

claim: Multi-task learning (noise prediction + segmentation mask) achieved 40% MPJPE reduction on hand keypoints; fine-tuning on narrow hand datasets causes catastrophic forgetting
quote: Publicly available datasets that include annotated hands often lack visual diversity and tend to concentrate only on hands without including the rest of the body.

claim: Counting hallucinations stem from mode interpolation and accumulated denoising errors; increasing sampling steps 25→100 worsens counting accuracy for hands; pixel-level constraints reduced hallucination rate ~23%
quote: Samples lie between incompatible modes, producing semantically invalid content. Increasing sampling steps exacerbates counting hallucinations in real hand images.

claim: Hand1000: models fail because CLIP lacks prior knowledge of hand physical structure and struggles with gesture-language alignment; fusing Mediapipe gesture features into text embeddings achieved 28.6-point FID-H improvement with only 1,000 training images
quote: The inherent complexity of the human hand's structure, along with the occlusions between fingers, means that the Stable Diffusion model lacks the necessary prior knowledge of the precise physical structure.

claim: ControlNet (33.9k stars) enables depth maps, pose maps, and edge signals to condition diffusion generation without retraining the base model
quote: ControlNet copies the weights of neural network blocks into a locked copy and a trainable copy, using zero convolutions to prevent distortion during training.

claim: DALL-E 3 trained a specialized captioner to generate long descriptive captions covering body parts, mixing 95% synthetic (GPT-4) with 5% human captions to prevent overfitting
quote: Fine-tuning on long, highly-descriptive captions describing the contents of each image including surroundings, background, styles, coloration, etc.

claim: SDXL uses dual text encoders (CLIP ViT-G + CLIP ViT-L) and native 1024×1024 resolution; U-Net has 2.6B parameters vs SD 1.5's 860M
quote: SDXL uses two encoders — OpenCLIP ViT-bigG and the original CLIP ViT-L — working in parallel. SDXL generates highly realistic human figures with accurate anatomy.

claim: FLUX's transformer architecture attends to all image parts simultaneously enabling consistent spatial relationships; SDXL's U-Net locality causes finger inconsistencies
quote: Transformers can attend to all parts of the image simultaneously, leading to more consistent compositions. SDXL still occasionally produces anatomical errors, particularly with hands.

claim: FLUX.1 produces the most anatomically correct humans with correct finger count in the vast majority of generations
quote: FLUX.1 demonstrates exceptional capability in generating text, adhering to intricate prompts, and accurately depicting human anatomy, particularly hands.

claim: Midjourney v5 fixed hands by explicitly prioritizing images with clearly visible hands and deprioritizing obscured examples in training data
quote: Midjourney updated its datasets to prioritize clearer hand images while deprioritizing those where hands are obscured or partially visible.

claim: At 512×512, Stable Diffusion cannot fill the detail needed for well-formed hands due to resolution constraints
quote: At small sizes like 512x512px, Stable Diffusion can't fill in the details needed for well-formed hands.

claim: Midjourney v6 was trained from scratch over nine months; v5 created 'better images, fewer nightmare hands'
quote: The model was trained from scratch over a nine month period. Support was added for better text rendition and a more literal interpretation of prompts.

claim: Midjourney v7 uses a complete ground-up model rebuild reporting ~40% reduction in anatomical errors; six-fingered hands moved from common to occasional
quote: A complete rebuild of the underlying model architecture. 40% reduction in anatomical errors with particular improvements in hands and faces.

claim: Success rates improved from ~30% (2022) to ~65% (MJ v5 2023) to ~75-80% (v6 2024) to ~85-90% (v7 2025)
quote: 2022: ~30% acceptable hands. 2023 Post-V5: ~65% acceptable. 2024 V6: ~75-80% acceptable. 2025 V7: ~85-90% acceptable.

claim: Midjourney v5 explicitly improved generation of hands, skin textures, and teeth with a new neural architecture trained on AI supercluster for ~5 months
quote: Midjourney Version 5 boasts several improvements, including improved resolution and photorealism, better generation of hands, skin textures, and teeth.

claim: SDXL is a 3.5B-parameter base model with 6.6B-parameter refiner operating at 1024×1024
quote: SDXL is an open-source text-to-image model. It is a 3.5B-parameter base model paired with a 6.6B-parameter refiner, making it one of the largest open-access image generation models.

claim: Midjourney v7 CEO David Holz described it as a totally different architecture from v6
quote: CEO David Holz called it a totally different architecture in the official announcement.
